questions.evidence:
In Class Nine, phones usually stay in a numbered box during lessons. A notice says students may retrieve a device for a learning task only when the teacher gives permission. The rule is meant to reduce interruptions without preventing a planned activity that needs a camera or timer.

During a science lesson, Dan sees Mina using her phone and says she is breaking the rule. Mina has been asked to photograph the group's model. Dan did not hear the instruction because he was helping carry materials from the storage room.

Instead of arguing about what must have happened, Dan asks the teacher to clarify. She explains the limited permission and reminds Mina to return the device after taking the pictures. The permission does not allow unrelated messaging during the rest of the lesson.

Later, the teacher writes the approved task and its ending point on the board. Dan apologizes for making a public accusation before checking the situation. A general rule still matters, but applying it fairly requires knowing whether a specific exception has actually been authorized.
questions.explanation: 先核對行為事實、許可範圍，再適用規則。
options: Making an accusation before asking about permission.
Removing every general rule after one exception.
Checking the facts and the limits of any authorized exception.
Assuming every visible phone use has the same purpose.
questions.prompt: What supports fair application of the rule?
